# aeneid-073 (X.96–184) — drafter's notes

43 units; `make_units.py` runs clean (no LINE COUNT / TOO LONG / NEWLINE / ENDING / NOTE LENGTH / MARK warnings). `t` comes
only from `A.cut`; no `sc`. Longest units are five lines (121b–125a, ending `prima acies;`) and four lines (132–135a,
139–142, 150b–153a, 159–162, 175–178). Paragraphs 96, 118, 146, 163, 166 all start a unit at line start and carry `p: true`;
each note opens "A new paragraph in Greenough."

Title `Iovis nutus. Classis Etrusca`; part "Jupiter's Nod and the Etruscan Fleet (X.96–184)".

## Speech marks

Jupiter: “ 104 (`“Accipite`) … ” 113 (misprint, below). One “ and one ” in each of t, l, i.

## Misprints

- 10.113 `invenient. ”Stygii` — closing mark joined to the next word. Unit is 113–115, ending `Olympum.` (3 lines), so the
  speech close and the narrative of the oath and nod share one unit; l and i close the speech after "find." Note opens
  "The print has 'invenient. ”Stygii', a misprint for 'invenient.” Stygii', corrected here; t keeps the print." (single
  quotes, as in 054/071 notes, rather than the backticks in the brief's wording — reviewer may change if the rule wants
  backticks literally).
- No other misprint found.

## Latin Library disagreements

All orthographic (volnera/uulnera, dirigere/derigere, moerorum/murorum, divom/diuum, Tercentum/ter centum) except the name
Astur/Astyr at 180–181, which is noted (same man, no change of sense). `moerorum` is glossed as Greenough's archaic
spelling of `murorum`. No bracketed lines in this part.

## Doubtful points

- 10.129 `fratre Menestheo`: Greenough (and LL, no disagreement) has `Menestheo`, while 143 has `Mnestheus`. Many texts read
  `Mnestheo` at 129. Kept as printed; the note reads it as Me-nes-theo with synizesis and does not identify the brother
  with the Mnestheus of 143. Scansion of the line should be checked when scan-fixes are done.
- 10.136 scanner flag (`inclusum buxo aut Oricia terebintho`): not my brief (no `sc`), but the hand-scan needs care: elision
  `bux(o) aut`, Greek `Oricia`, four-syllable Greek ending. The note only says "a Greek rhythm"; reviewer may wish to say
  more once the scansion is fixed.
- 10.109–110 `Seu… sive…`: elliptical; i supplies "It is all one whether…". Interpretation of `monitis sinistris` as
  "warnings misread / ill-starred" is a judgement call.
- 10.154 `libera fati`: taken as "freed from the bar of fate" (the oracle requiring a foreign leader, Book VIII).
- 10.184 `intempestae`: rendered "unwholesome / fever-ridden", following the old explanation (feverish air).
- 10.167 `mille manus iuvenum`: taken as "a band of a thousand young men".

## Attributions from memory (please verify)

- Georgics 1.356–359 as the weather-sign parallel to the simile at 97–99.
- Iliad 1.528–530 (Zeus's nod shakes Olympus).
- 113b–115 repeat IX.104b–106 (checked against the edition: 9.104–106 match).
- 163 repeats VII.641 (checked against the edition: identical).
- Iliad 2.484–493, invocation before the Catalogue of Ships.
- Hicetaon as Priam's brother in the Iliad.
- Sarpedon killed by Patroclus, Iliad 16.
- Iliad 5.302–304, Diomedes' stone "two men of later days could not carry".
- Capys among Aeneas's captains at I.183 (checked in the edition); Trojan Abas at I.121 (checked).
- Capua named from Capys; Etruscan Pisa founded from Pisa in Elis; Pactolus gold; Chalybes as iron-workers; Oricum and
  terebinth; Populonia facing Elba; Caere as Mezentius's city; Pyrgi as Caere's port; Minio a river of southern Etruria.

## Scope

The brief lists Cinyras, Cupavo, Ocnus, Aulestes; they fall after 184 (next part). This part ends with Astur's contingent
(Caere, Minio, Pyrgi, Graviscae); the last note and the ABOUT say the catalogue continues.
